source.author: lucan
source.text: Sic funere primo Attonitae tacuere domus, cum corpora nondum Conclamata iacent, nec mater crine soluto Exigit ad saevos famularum brachia planctus: Sed cum membra premit fugiente rigentia vita, Vultusque exanimes, oculosque in morte natantes, Necdum est ille dolor, sed iam metus: incubat amens, Miraturque malum.
source.text_original: Sic funere primo / Attonitae tacuere domus, cum corpora nondum / Conclamata iacent, nec mater crine soluto / Exigit ad saevos famularum brachia planctus: / Sed cum membra premit fugiente rigentia vita, / Vultusque exanimes, oculosque in morte natantes, / Necdum est ille dolor, sed iam metus: incubat amens, / Miraturque malum.
source.text_english: So at the first funeral the stupefied house was silent, when the bodies lie still, not yet duly lamented, and the mother does not with loose hair strain her arms in the servants’ savage wailing; but when the stiffening limbs are weighed down as life flees, and the faces are lifeless, and the eyes swimming in death, then there is not yet grief, but already fear: she bends over them in madness and marvels at the calamity.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: sin aliud Fortuna parat, miserere parentum, Mors bona, dum metus est nec adhuc dolor.
reuse.text_original: sin aliud Fortuna parat, miserere parentum, / Mors bona, dum metus est nec adhuc dolor.
reuse.text_english: But if Fortune is preparing something else, have pity on my parents, gentle Death, while there is still fear and not yet pain.
